To model the evaporation of LOX droplets, the convection/diffusion controlled model
based on a classical hydrodynamical models [59,60] was used to calculate the detachment
of molecules from the surface of LOX droplet to the bulk phase of GCH4 in the immediate
vicinity of droplets and diffusion of vapour from the droplet surface into the gaseous phase.
The assumption in this model is that the total density of the mixture of gas and droplet
vapour is constant in the vicinity of the droplet surface. The rate of droplet evaporation,

_m_ ˙ _d_ is expressed as,

_m_ ˙ _d_ = _kcAd_ _ρln(_ 1 + _Bm)_ (16)

where _kc_ is mass transfer coefficient (m/s), _Ad_ is droplet surface area (m <sup>2</sup> ), and _Bm_ is the
Spalding mass number based on the vapour mass fraction at the surface and in the bulk
gas. The combustion chamber wall was assumed as adiabatic thereby the heat flux was null
